passage:
Friday, after school. Today I sat with Tara at lunch for the first time! She has the best pencil case. I wanted her to like me, so I whispered, “I know a secret.” Then I told her Nilesh still sleeps with a night-light. Tara's eyes went big and she said, “Really? You know so much!” I felt so special, like I gave her a present.

Then Tara told Kabir, and Kabir laughed. Nilesh was standing by the water cooler, and I saw him go quiet and walk away with his bottle. I don't know why. Maybe he was thirsty.

Tara says we can sit together again on Monday.
— Pema

qa.q: What did Pema tell Tara about Nilesh?
qa.a: Pema told Tara that Nilesh still sleeps with a night-light.

qa.q: What was Pema feeling when Tara said, “You know so much!”?
qa.a: Pema felt happy and special, as if the secret were a present given to someone new.

qa.q: What could Pema do on Monday about what happened at the water cooler?
qa.a: Pema could check on Nilesh and say sorry for sharing the secret, before sitting with Tara again.

qa.q: What might Nilesh have felt, going quiet at the water cooler and walking away?
qa.a: Nilesh probably felt embarrassed and betrayed, hearing a private thing laughed at by people Nilesh had not told.

grounding: A child shares another child's secret to feel special and closer to someone new, without seeing the betrayal to the one it concerns.

passage:
At the village school's handpump, Kashish held the tin cup and looked at Leela, who had just come from the next village and knew nobody. Kashish wanted Leela's friendship. “I'll tell you a secret,” Kashish whispered. “Kishore practises singing in the cowshed. He's too scared to sing in class.”

Leela's eyes lit up. “Really? Say it again!” Kashish felt warm, as if giving a present. Two other girls leaned in, then giggled.

That afternoon, when the teacher asked who would sing for annual day, Kishore shook his head fast and kept his eyes on the floor. The giggles started again at the back. Kashish smiled at Leela and did not look at Kishore.

qa.a: Kishore practises singing in the cowshed.

qa.q: How did Kashish feel when Leela's eyes lit up at the secret?
qa.a: Kashish felt warm and pleased, as if giving a present, because Kashish wanted Leela's friendship.

qa.q: What could Kashish do after seeing Kishore refuse to sing?
qa.a: Kashish could tell Kishore sorry for sharing the secret and ask the girls to stop giggling.

qa.q: What might Kishore have felt when the giggles started at the back?
qa.a: Kishore probably felt exposed and hurt, realising a private fear had been passed around.

grounding: A child shares another's secret at a handpump to feel special and closer to someone new, without seeing the betrayal to the one it concerns.
